routes.label: Interpret the sum of four side lengths

question: If \(a\) represents the side length of a square (unit: cm), what does the algebraic expression \(4a\) represent for this square?
solution: A square has 4 sides, each of length \(a\). The sum of the side lengths, \(4a\), is its perimeter. Its area should be \(a^2\).

edges.reason: Written columns support perimeter arithmetic with larger dimensions. Adding decomposed lengths mentally gives the same result even for two-digit sides, so Gemini's chosen calculation does not establish column-method necessity.
The perimeter formulas use rectangle opposite-side equality and square side equality to combine their boundary lengths.
Two-digit columns support larger numerical areas. Repeated unit-square counts or decomposed multiplication can also compute an area, so no fixed dimension range is imposed by this preparation link.
edges.scope: computing areas with two-digit side lengths

edges.reason: The rectangle/square area formulas count equal square units, so the meaning of area and its uniform unit are part of the asserted result.
